```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>", error = FALSE)
```

`ysx_factors()` extends `yspec::ys_factors()` with per-variable ordering through
`dots$order`. It converts coded values to labelled factors while retaining the
original values in columns ending in `_v` by default.

## Specify the order in YAML

Set `order` to `first` to keep the level order defined in the specification,
or `biggest` to sort levels by decreasing frequency in the data being converted.
Omitting `order` is equivalent to `first`. No other values are accepted.

```yaml
SETUP__:
  description: Example factor ordering
RESPONSE:
  values: {Low: 1, Medium: 2, High: 3, Unused: 4}
  dots: {order: first}
```

The following example creates and loads this specification. In a project, pass
the path to your existing YAML file to `yspec::ys_load()` instead.

```{r specification}
library(yspecx)

spec_path <- tempfile(fileext = ".yaml")
yaml::write_yaml(
  list(
    SETUP__ = list(description = "Example factor ordering"),
    RESPONSE = list(
      values = list(Low = 1, Medium = 2, High = 3, Unused = 4),
      dots = list(order = "first")
    )
  ),
  spec_path
)
spec <- yspec::ys_load(spec_path)
unlink(spec_path)

data <- data.frame(ID = seq_len(7), RESPONSE = c(3, 2, 2, 3, 2, 1, NA))
```

## Preserve specification order

`first` refers to specification order, not the order of first appearance in the
data. Here `High` appears first in the data, but `Low` is the first factor level.

```{r first}
first <- ysx_factors(data, spec)
levels(first$RESPONSE)
head(first)
```

## Order from biggest to smallest

Change the setting in the YAML file, or update the loaded specification:

```{r biggest}
spec$RESPONSE$dots$order <- "biggest"
biggest <- ysx_factors(data, spec)
levels(biggest$RESPONSE)
table(biggest$RESPONSE, useNA = "ifany")
```

`Medium` occurs three times, `High` twice and `Low` once. The unused level remains
last. Missing observations do not contribute to these counts unless they are an
explicit factor level. The underlying observations are not sorted or changed;
only the level order changes.

Frequencies are calculated from the data supplied to each call. If levels have
equal counts, their relative order follows the original yspec factor order.

```{r ties}
tied <- ysx_factors(data.frame(RESPONSE = c(3, 2)), spec)
levels(tied$RESPONSE)
```

Although `High` appears first, `Medium` precedes it because they have equal
counts and `Medium` comes first in the specification. Unused levels also keep
their relative specification order.

## Select columns and retain original values

Column selection and value-column options follow `yspec::ys_factors()`.
Pass unquoted column names to restrict conversion. Use `.keep_values = FALSE`
to omit the original codes, or `.suffix` to choose their column suffix.

```{r options}
selected <- ysx_factors(data, spec, RESPONSE, .keep_values = FALSE)
names(selected)

with_codes <- ysx_factors(data, spec, RESPONSE, .suffix = "_code")
head(with_codes)
```

## Existing factors and validation

Existing factor columns are left unchanged, including their level order. To
change the ordering after a previous conversion, call `ysx_factors()` on the
original coded data rather than the factor output.

```{r existing-factors}
unchanged <- ysx_factors(first, spec)
identical(levels(unchanged$RESPONSE), levels(first$RESPONSE))
```

An invalid `dots$order` setting raises an error when that variable is converted.
Settings on unselected variables or existing factors are not validated.
